questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Time Specificity: Night with Adjective Modifier
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The special judicial notification was issued late ___ the night of 14th August."
questions.explanation: General rule mein 'at night' hota hai, lekin jab 'night' ke sath koi specific calendar date ya day ka reference jud jata hai ('the night of 14th August'), toh formula badal kar strictly 'ON' ho jata hai: 'on the night of 14th August'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Time Preposition Pyramid — ON for specific calendar nights and modified day-parts.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Place Preposition: In vs At Spatial Coordinate Concord
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The permanent bench of the High Court is situated ___ Jodhpur ___ Rajasthan."
questions.explanation: Jab do geographical entities ka hierarchy comparison ho, toh comparatively smaller city/district ke pehle 'AT' aur larger territory/state ke pehle 'IN' lagta hai: 'at Jodhpur in Rajasthan'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Place Preposition Matrix — Chhote location ke sath 'AT' aur bade area ke sath 'IN'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The clerk crumpled the defective petition and tossed it ___ the wastepaper basket."
questions.explanation: Action verb 'tossed' (fehnka) exterior se kisi 3D hollow container ke andar dynamic movement show kar raha hai. Boundary cross karke interior mein landing ke liye strictly 'INTO' lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: In vs Into — INTO for dynamic action directing an object into an enclosure.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The protestor climbed ___ the roof of the administrative building to raise slogans."
questions.explanation: Verb 'climbed' upward dynamic movement show kar raha hai jo person ko open flat surface ('the roof') ke upar lekar aati hai. Surface landing movement ke liye strictly 'ONTO' lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: On vs Onto — ONTO for movement landing on an elevated surface.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the correct preposition:
"The police van proceeded ___ the High Court, but was diverted to the central jail en route."
questions.explanation: Kyunki police van High Court nahi pahunchi aur raste mein hi divert ho gayi, isliye destination reached ('to') ungrammatical ho gaya. Sirf directional heading ('TOWARDS') logically aur grammatically valid hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: To vs Towards — TOWARDS indicates directional heading without destination guarantee.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The junior advocate hurried ___ the crowded corridor to reach Courtroom Number 4."
questions.explanation: 'The crowded corridor' ek 3D space/passage hai jo logon aur deewaron se surrounded hai. Aise enclosed passage ya bheed ke andar se nikalne ke liye preposition 'THROUGH' use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Movement Vectors — THROUGH for passing inside an enclosed passage, crowd, or conduit.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The Division Bench ordered that all replies must be filed in the registry ___ 4:00 PM tomorrow."
questions.explanation: Action verb 'filed' point-action event hai aur '4:00 PM tomorrow' cut-off deadline (not later than) mark kar raha hai. Filing deadline ke liye strictly 'BY' use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: By vs Until — BY indicates deadline threshold for point-action verbs.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The arguments of the learned senior counsel continued ___ the evening recess was called."
questions.explanation: Verb 'continued' ek durative ongoing action hai jo evening recess tak lagaatar chalta raha. Ongoing duration terminating at an event strictly 'UNTIL' demand karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: By vs Until — UNTIL marks ongoing duration up to a specified terminal event.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The System Assistant has been managing the e-filing portal ___ 2018."
questions.explanation: '2018' ek specific starting point of time (calendar year) hai jahan se action shuru hokar present tak continue ho raha hai ('has been managing'). Point in time ke pehle strictly 'SINCE' lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Since vs For — SINCE with exact starting calendar points.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Time Duration: For with Measured Period
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The committee has been deliberating on the service rules ___ seven consecutive hours."
questions.explanation: 'Seven consecutive hours' ek measured duration (quantity of time) hai. Total duration of time ke pehle strictly 'FOR' use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Since vs For — FOR with periods of measured duration.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses the preposition:
A) The boundary dispute was amicably resolved among the States of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
B) The boundary dispute was amicably resolved between the States of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
C) The boundary dispute was amicably resolved amidst the States of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
D) The boundary dispute was amicably resolved with the States of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
questions.explanation: Jab 3 ya usse zyada individual sovereign states ya parties individually named ho aur unke beech mutual/reciprocal border settlement ya relationship ho, toh standard English rule strictly 'BETWEEN' demand karta hai. Sentence (B) 100% correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Between vs Among — BETWEEN for 3+ distinct, individually named entities in mutual relation.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Group Distribution: Among with Collective Pool
questions.question:
Fill in the blank:
"The welfare compensation was distributed equitably ___ the families of the deceased workers."
questions.explanation: Receiver 'the families of the deceased workers' ek plural collective pool hai (undifferentiated group). Collective group distribution ke liye strictly 'AMONG' use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Between vs Among — AMONG for collective, undifferentiated groups of 3+ members.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"The Chief Justice / discussed about the pendency of criminal appeals / with all administrative judges / yesterday afternoon."

options.text: discussed about the pendency of criminal appeals

questions.explanation: Part (B) mein 'discussed about' galat hai. 'Discuss' direct transitive verb hai jiska matlab 'talk about' hota hai. Iske baad 'about' lagana redundant pleonasm hai. Correct: 'discussed the pendency of criminal appeals'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Zero Preposition Law — 'Discuss' takes a direct object without 'about'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"No unauthorized person / is permitted to / enter into the server room / without biometric authorization."
questions.explanation: Part (C) mein 'enter into the server room' likha hai. Physical room ya enclosure mein entry ke liye verb 'enter' ke baad 'into' lagana strictly ungrammatical hai. Correct phrasing hai: 'enter the server room'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Zero Preposition Law — 'Enter' takes NO preposition for physical spaces.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
A) The judicial delegation reached to Jaipur at midnight.
B) The judicial delegation reached at Jaipur at midnight.
C) The judicial delegation reached Jaipur at midnight.
D) The judicial delegation reached into Jaipur at midnight.
questions.explanation: Verb 'reach' direct transitive verb hai jiska matlab hota hai 'arrive at'. Iske baad preposition 'to', 'at', ya 'into' lagana redundant error hai. Direct object aayega: 'reached Jaipur'. Sentence (C) 100% correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Zero Preposition Law — 'Reach' takes a direct object without 'to' or 'at'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L11 Certification
